definition: Detecting candidate lung nodules in CT scans — the first stage of automated lung screening pipelines.
details: Detecting candidate lung nodules in CT scans — the first stage of automated lung screening pipelines.

explainer.lead: Lung nodule detection finds candidate nodules in CT scans so that automated lung screening pipelines have something to examine. It matters because it is the first stage of those pipelines, deciding what later stages get to assess.

tiers.eli5: It is like scanning a big beach with a metal detector to mark every spot worth digging up, before anyone decides which spots are treasure.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers build it as the candidate-generating front end of a screening pipeline, so its output feeds later stages rather than being the final answer. The pitfall is treating candidates as findings.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally it is the detection stage of an automated lung screening pipeline: given a CT scan, output candidate lung nodules. The given facts do not specify a formula or its performance limits.

explainer.example: A CT scan passes through the detection stage, which marks candidate nodules; those candidates then go on to the rest of the screening pipeline.
